## 1. One-paragraph verdict
A real ffmpeg-generated VP9-in-IVF fixture whose header decodes exactly as the
filename promises (manual decode from bytes: DKIF, version 0, hdrlen 32, fourcc
`VP90`, width 64, height 48, rate 25, scale 1, 25 frames). It carries the
strongest pinning of this batch: the demuxed packet-stream payload_md5 is
pinned against `ffmpeg -c copy -f md5` (e62f0aba…), and a dated compat-matrix
row records the full DECODE (25/25 frames) — not just demux. The fuzz corpus
twin is byte-identical (cmp).

## 3. Findings
F-001 [S4]
Where: tests/fixtures/generated/MANIFEST.toml (absence of ivf rows)
Code: `rg 'ivf' tests/fixtures/generated/MANIFEST.toml -> No matches found`
What is wrong: the ivf family (2 files) is unregistered in the MANIFEST drift
gate — no sha256/size pin. Severity S4 (not the S3 of the ogg/webm/mp4_h264_aac
families) because this family's behavioral pins are md5-strength: ANY payload
byte drift changes the pinned payload_md5 and fails ivf_fixtures; only
cosmetic drift in non-parsed header bytes (e.g. the reserved u32 at bytes
28-31) could pass silently, and the pinned hdrlen/params would catch most of
that too.
What correct looks like: MANIFEST rows for both ivf fixtures (cheap; closes the
cosmetic-drift hole).
Confidence: HIGH — Verification: read (rg executed, zero hits) + md5-pin
reasoning over the green test.
